# 🌙 CoreNap

> **Cores take a nap when your screen does.**

CoreNap parks a selectable number of CPU cores while your display is off, caps the remaining awake cores at a frequency you choose, and wakes everything back up the moment you unlock. Watch it happen live from the built-in WebUI core map.

---

## ✨ Features

- 💤 **Auto-park on screen off** — up to `N` of the highest (fastest) cores go offline when you lock your phone
- 🔢 **You choose how many** — 1 to all pinnable cores, straight from the WebUI stepper
- ⚡ **Frequency cap for awake cores** — clamp the remaining cores to any supported frequency (big.LITTLE aware, per-cluster clamping)
- 🔋 **Charging-aware** — optionally skip parking while plugged in for faster charging and less heat
- 🚀 **Boot grace period** — never parks during the first minute after boot or before your first unlock
- 🔓 **Wake on unlock** — optionally wake **every** core on unlock, or restore only what CoreNap parked
- 🗺️ **Live core map** — WebUI tiles refresh every 2s: awake / napping / offline state + real-time per-core frequency bars
- 🐕 **Watchdog protected** — a supervisor revives the watcher if it ever dies; screen checks are timeout-guarded so a wedged system can never freeze it
- 🔒 **Safe by design** — `cpu0` is never parked, every sysfs write is verified, caps are always removed on wake/disable/uninstall
- 🖥️ **Full terminal menu** — everything the WebUI does, available over adb/Termux

## 📦 Installation

1. Download the latest zip from [Releases](https://github.com/MiniVoidyy/CoreNap-/releases) (or build it yourself)
2. Flash in **Magisk**, **KernelSU**, **KernelSU Next**, **SukiSU** or **APatch**
3. Reboot
4. Open the module's **WebUI** from your manager app

## 🎛️ Usage

### WebUI
Open CoreNap in your manager app → WebUI:
- Stepper (`− N +`) → how many cores to park
- Frequency dropdown → cap for the awake cores
- Toggle → wake-every-core on unlock
- Park now / Wake all / Enable / Restart watcher buttons

### Terminal
```bash
su -c sh /data/adb/corenap/scripts/corenap.sh menu      # interactive menu
```

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `on` / `off` / `toggle` | enable / disable |
| `set <N>` | park `<N>` cores |
| `freq <kHz\|max>` | frequency cap for awake cores |
| `wakeall-mode true/false` | wake every core vs only parked ones |
| `interval <s>` | screen check interval (1–3600s) |
| `park` / `wakeall` | manual park / wake |
| `status` | banner + live ASCII core map |
| `json` | machine-readable status (used by WebUI) |

## ⚙️ Configuration

Everything lives in one file — also linked at the bottom of the WebUI:

```
/data/adb/corenap/config.conf
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ENABLED` | `true` | master switch |
| `PARK_COUNT` | `4` | cores to park while screen is off |
| `WAKE_ALL_ON_UNLOCK` | `true` | wake *every* core on unlock |
| `SCAN_INTERVAL` | `2` | seconds between screen-state checks |
| `CAP_FREQ` | `0` | max kHz for awake cores (`0` = no cap) |
| `SKIP_CHARGING` | `false` | don't park while charging |

The watcher re-reads this file every tick — edits apply live, no restart needed.

## 🔬 How it works

1. A lightweight watcher polls screen state (`dumpsys deviceidle`, with `dumpsys power` fallback and hard timeouts)
2. Screen **off** → writes `0` to `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/online` for the top N cores, then clamps `scaling_max_freq` on the survivors
3. Screen **on** → brings cores back, restores hardware max frequencies
4. A watchdog revives the watcher if anything kills it; all park/wake mutations are lock-serialized against manual WebUI actions

## ✅ Verify it works

```bash
# watch cores vanish when the screen goes off
adb shell "while true; do cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/online; sleep 1; done"

# module status + log
adb shell "su -c 'sh /data/adb/corenap/scripts/corenap.sh status'"
adb shell "su -c 'tail -f /data/adb/corenap/log.txt'"
```

## 🧯 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `watcher: stopped` in status | `su -c ... corenap.sh watcher-restart` (watchdog will also self-heal within 30s) |
| `FAILED to park cpuX (kernel refused)` | Your kernel pins that cluster online — lower the park count |
| Cores come back on their own | ROM thermal/hotplug driver re-onlining them; normal on some devices, CoreNap re-parks next tick |
| WebUI shows dashes | Open it **from the manager app**, grant the module WebUI/root permission |

## 🤝 Compatibility

| Manager | Supported |
|---|---|
| Magisk | ✅ |
| KernelSU | ✅ |
| KernelSU Next | ✅ |
| SukiSU | ✅ |
| APatch | ✅ |

---

**CoreNap V1** · by [Mini_Voidyy](https://github.com/MiniVoidyy) · sleep tight, little cores 😴
